dialogues.speaker: Uncle Ghast
dialogues.text: Oh? Come and have a chat, kid. Who knows — if the influence of those meteorites gets any stronger, there'll be no one to talk to but in your dreams. *chuckles*

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Ghast
dialogues.text: Hehe, the brats in the village call me Uncle Ghast, for I am never without a ghost story to tell.

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Ghast
dialogues.text: Well, would like you to hear a story too? Well then, ground yourself well, lest a single scare sets your legs to trembling!

response.speaker: Uncle Ghast
response.text: There was once a young lass called Dusky Ming, a cute and precocious girl, but one whose luck was poor. She suffered from a terrible illness, and died young.

response.speaker: Uncle Ghast
response.text: Her mother washed her face with tears, and would not leave the house, for the blow was too much for her to bear.

response.speaker: Uncle Ghast
response.text: But one day, there was a knock, knock, knock at their door. Frightened, her mother carefully pushed the door open...

response.speaker: Uncle Ghast
response.text: ...and when she looked, there was a piping hot bowl of meat soup and a plate of cooked meat, but not a soul in sight. Not comprehending this, Dusky Ming's mother followed the trail of that wonderful aroma...

response.speaker: Uncle Ghast
response.text: Only to stumble right into a hilichurl camp. Quickly they surrounded her, and oh, how her eyes grew wide with fright.

response.speaker: Uncle Ghast
response.text: But the moment passed, and all she heard was the chanting of "Dada... Dada..." The mother opened her eyes as quickly as she dared, and what did she see?

response.speaker: Uncle Ghast
response.text: The hilichurls dancing, dancing Dusky Ming's favorite dance!

response.speaker: Uncle Ghast
response.text: Just then, she felt something bump into her from behind, and though she could see no one, she could smell a familiar fragrance.

response.speaker: Uncle Ghast
response.text: Tears rolled down the mother's face, for then she knew that her Dusky Ming was not lonely in the afterlife, no indeed — she had instead made herself many an adorable friend...

response.speaker: Uncle Ghast
response.text: What are you babbling about? Dusky Ming is a ghost — is that not enough to frighten folk?

response.speaker: Uncle Ghast
response.text: How does your mind even tick...

response.speaker: Uncle Ghast
response.text: Hehe... This is the ghost story I am most proud of, after all. It has never failed me yet!

response.speaker: Uncle Ghast
response.text: Most important of all, this story is real as real can be.

response.speaker: Uncle Ghast
response.text: Hmph. And here I thought you would have a little more guts than those brats.

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Ghast
dialogues.text: As you please, youngster. If you ever want to hear another story, come and find me any time.
